title: My backtest wins 80% of the time. Here’s how it still loses money.
author: Electrical_Waltz_888
selftext:
Imagine two backtests, each with 100 trades:

* **Strategy A:** 80 wins averaging $25, 20 losses averaging $120. Total: **−$400** before costs.
* **Strategy B:** 40 wins averaging $150, 60 losses averaging $70. Total: **+$1,800** before costs.

These are made-up numbers, but they show why “80% win rate” tells you so little on its own. I’d want to know how much the winners make, how much the losers cost, and whether a handful of trades account for most of the profit.

Here’s an AI prompt you can use with a backtest export:

>Using only the trades I provide, calculate the average win, average loss and average net result per trade. Show the arithmetic so I can check it. Then show how much of the net profit came from the five biggest winners. If fees or slippage aren’t recorded, say what’s missing rather than guessing.

Removing the biggest winners is a sensitivity check. Some strategies are designed around rare big wins, so the point is to understand what the result depends on.

What’s the first number you look at when someone posts a high win rate?

Disclosure: I’m the author of *The Complete Guide to AI Powered Trading*. It covers how to question backtest results and includes 50 reusable AI prompts.

[Find the book on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HNM97TQ9)

comments.body: Is it available in a digital form I can feed to my AI?

replies.author: Electrical_Waltz_888
replies.body:
Yep, it’s available on Kindle: [https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HNM97TQ9](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HNM97TQ9)

If you mean uploading the whole book to your AI as a file, the Kindle edition isn’t a standalone PDF. It does include 50 prompts designed to use individually with your own trading rules, backtest results or journal entries.
